sentences.text: Referring to this 164 statement, it is submitted that the appellant/accused was only 21 years of age at the time of commission of offence and that he has already served more than 03 years out of the 15 years sentence that has been imposed upon him.
It is further stated that he has no criminal antecedents.

3. The application is opposed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, who submits that even assuming that there was consent on part of the victim, she being under 18 years of age, the offence would certainly be made out.
4. Heard both sides.
5. As stated earlier, I was taken through the entire 164 statement of the victim in this case.
The accused/appellant was only 21 years of age at the time of the commission of offence and has no criminal antecedents.
The appeal is of the year 2025 and so there is no possibility of it being heard in near future.
Hence, in these facts and circumstances of the case, the sentence of the This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 30/01/2026 at 20:47:48 appellant is suspended during the pendency of the appeal on executing a personal bond of 15,000/- with two solvent sureties for the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial court,
subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall not commit any offence(s) while on bail and shall appear before this Court as and when directed.
(ii) The appellant shall provide his mobile number and residential address to the Station House Officer (SHO) concerned, on which he shall remain available.
In case of change of his mobile number or residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the SHO concerned as well as this Court.
(iii) Needless to say, in the event of violation of any of the aforementioned condition(s), the suspension of sentence granted shall forthwith stand cancelled.
6. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
